source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
The booklet gives a spacing diagram (labeled 'watermelon planting model') showing two parallel rows of planting points on a bed layout.

As read from the diagram: spacing between individual plants within a row is 0.5 meter; the distance marked between the two planting rows is shown as 3 meters; and an outer distance spanning the bed/furrow system is marked as 5 meters; a further 1-meter measurement is marked along the top of the layout.

Note on reading the figure: the diagram uses stacked arrows (1 m, 5 m, 3 m, and 0.5 m) whose exact reference lines are not fully explicit in the scanned image — the 0.5 m clearly marks in-row plant spacing, but which of the 1 m / 3 m / 5 m values represents row-to-row spacing versus bed-to-bed (furrow) spacing is visually ambiguous and should be double-checked against the original diagram or with a local agronomist before being used as a firm recommendation. What is reliably certain from the figure is that watermelon is planted in a double-row (paired-row) layout on each bed, with wide aisles left between bed units for vine spreading and access.
